title: Intercom developer FAQs
snippet:
Use this article to set up your Intercom developer environment, configure a custom Help Center domain with SSL, authenticate your app via access tokens or OAuth, and manage contacts, conversations, and tickets via the Intercom API (Application Programming Interface). It also covers webhooks, pagination, building Messenger and Inbox apps, and troubleshooting common API and SSL errors.

If you are getting a 403 API Plan restricted message in a response this means that the API you are trying to use is not available on your app's plan.
In order to access the API you'll need to upgrade your plan. You can find out more about Intercom plans[ on this page](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/8420845-intercom-plans-explained). You can find a full list of[ error codes](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/error-codes/) and[ HTTP responses](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/http-responses/) in our developer documentation.

## What type of authentication is required for public apps?
Any apps that interact with third party workspace data and apps built with Canvas Kit require OAuth to be in place. You should never ask users for their access token and only use OAuth for interacting with their data.
## Do I have to use OAuth for my app?
You'll need to set up OAuth if you're building an integration with Intercom that accesses other peoples' Intercom data. This includes public apps that you plan to list on the Intercom app store as well as apps and integrations you will ask users to install through your own website. Learn more about OAuth from[ our developer documentation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/#oauth).
If you are only accessing data within you own Intercom workspace you can use an[ access token](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/#access-tokens).

To find your API access token, follow these steps:
1. Open the **Intercom Developer Hub**.
2. Navigate to **Your Apps** at Developer Hub > Settings > Your Apps. You should see a list of apps associated with your workspace.
3. Locate your private app, which may include your workspace’s name and sometimes the suffix "Access Token App."
4. Click the app name to open its details.
5. Go to the **Authentication** section to find the token. Treat this token like a password, as it is private and should not be shared.
